researcher_notes:
Checked all 93 assigned backlog rows (81 unique source URLs after de-duplication -- many rows shared a URL because the original 2026-07-21 crawler pattern-matched the same page against multiple brand-name guesses). 49 of the 93 rows confirmed a real, named vendor-customer relationship; those 49 rows collapsed into 46 distinct vendor+brand records below because a handful of brands (P.F. Chang's, California Fish Grill, Freebirds World Burrito) were independently corroborated by two source URLs each, which I merged into single richer records rather than duplicating. 44 rows were rejected. Zero rows were dead/unreachable -- every URL resolved to a live page; all rejections were 'not a real relationship for the guessed brand' rather than broken links. Zero rows are unchecked (full 93/93 coverage achieved).

Common rejection patterns observed, roughly in order of frequency:
1. URL-slug word-collision false positives, where the crawler matched a substring rather than the actual brand: the single biggest cluster was 'Pizza Press, The' (19 rows), which the crawler matched against 19 different Paytronix 'news-press/press-releases/...' URLs purely because the word 'press' appears in the URL path -- none of those 19 pages (about Jamba Juice, Illegal Pete's, JINYA Ramen Bar, UNO Pizzeria & Grill, Anthony's Coal Fired Pizza, Walk-On's, King's Classic, Quality Oil Company, and several vendor-to-vendor technology-partnership announcements with no restaurant brand at all) mention 'Pizza Press' anywhere. Similarly 'Stand Restaurants, The' and 'Taco Stand, The' (10 rows combined) were matched to generic Thanx/Paytronix blog and help-center articles about loyalty concepts merely because the word 'stand'/'stands' appears in the title (e.g. 'Where Customer Loyalty Stands Today,' 'How Great Loyalty Programs Stand Out From the Rest') -- none of those pages name either brand. 'Ward's Restaurant' (3 rows) was similarly matched to generic Thanx blog posts about 're-wards' programs and a Chipotle Chiptopia competitor-analysis post, with no actual mention of 'Ward's.' 'California Pizza Kitchen' and 'Calif Chicken Cafe' (4 rows combined) were matched to two Olo case studies that are genuinely about a different, real Olo customer, 'California Fish Grill,' via the shared word 'California'/'Calif.' 'Chicken Express' and one 'Pizza Press' row were matched to an Olo case study that is genuinely about a convenience-store chain called 'Family Express,' via the shared word 'Express.' 'Daily Grill' (2 rows) was matched to Paytronix content that is genuinely about a different, real customer named 'Twice Daily' (a convenience-store/foodservice brand), via the shared word 'Daily.'
2. Competitor/thought-leadership analysis, not a real customer, exactly as flagged in the task brief: 'Buffalo Wild Wings' and 'Wild Wing Cafe' (2 rows, same URL) both pointed to a Thanx blog post that critiques Buffalo Wild Wings' own in-house 'Blazin' Rewards' program as a cautionary example -- the post never claims BWW uses Thanx, and Wild Wing Cafe is not mentioned at all.
3. Page exists and names the vendor but never confirms a customer relationship: the Sweetfin/Thanx row pointed to a COVID-era podcast interview that Thanx produced as editorial content but that never states Sweetfin uses Thanx's product.
4. Generic partner-directory page with no restaurant brand named at all: the Pizza Ranch/Paytronix row pointed to a Paytronix partner-directory listing for a franchise-consulting firm (SL Franchise Group) with no restaurant brand named anywhere on the page.

On the confirmed side, evidence quality was generally strong: most Olo and Qu records include explicit unit counts and/or 'systemwide'/'all locations' language sufficient for a brand_wide_deployment classification; several Thanx and Paytronix records include named executive quotes and quantified results but lack unit counts, so those were conservatively scored deployed_scope_not_publicly_disclosed. One record (World of Beer Bar & Kitchen / Paytronix) is dated 2018 and flagged historical_current_status_not_reconfirmed given the brand's ownership changes since then. One brand-name correction was made: the backlog crawler's guess 'Honest Restaurant' actually resolves to a real Thanx customer named 'Honest Mary's' -- the corrected name is used in that record.
